- Model consistently underestimates prices, especially in early days of the 30-day forecast horizon.
- Forecasts tend to be too low in the first 5–10 days, then gradually increase — suggesting a lag in capturing short-term price momentum.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., 79.80 → 80.30 → 81.45), model overreacts and overshoots, then corrects — indicating sensitivity to recent volatility without proper mean reversion.
- Model exhibits persistent downward bias in the middle of the forecast, particularly around day 15–20, where true values are higher.
- Forecasts often fail to capture the “rebound” after a dip — e.g., after 75.21, model predicts 75.01 or 74.74, while true value rebounds to 76.17 or 76.46.
- Model tends to overestimate the “tail” of the forecast (last 5–7 days), especially when true values are trending upward — suggesting overconfidence in short-term continuation.
- Mean reversion is not adequately modeled — model holds onto low forecasts too long, even when recent history shows upward momentum.
- Forecasts are overly conservative in the early part of the horizon, underestimating the “recovery” phase after a dip.
